title: Deep Review Fix
description: One finding fixed inside a Phase 5 batch, plus the Phase 6 review that was appended to it. PRODUCER: Phase 5 fix lanes (05-fixes/<batch>.json), which write everything EXCEPT `review`; Phase 6 reviewers (06-fix-reviews/<batch>.json) re-emit the same object with `review` populated. CONSUMERS: Phase 6 (reads finding_id, files_touched, pre_fix_sha to compute the diff it reviews), Phase 10 (reads review verdicts when ranking what already landed). FILE SHAPE: both artifacts are collection.schema.json envelopes whose `items` are these objects — this schema validates one element, not the file. A fixer never writes `review`; a reviewer never edits the fields below it. That split is what stops an agent marking its own homework.

finding_id.description: Joins to finding.schema.json id and verdict.schema.json finding_id. The verdict MUST have disposition 'auto-fix'; Phase 5 fixing anything else is a protocol violation.

files_touched.description: Repo-relative paths this fix actually modified. MUST be a subset of the lane's scope fence — a path outside it is scope creep and fails Phase 6.

mutations_applied.description: How many discrete edits the lane made for this finding. 0 means the lane changed nothing and MUST say why in `notes` — a silent no-op is the failure mode where a batch reports green having done nothing.

pre_fix_sha.description: The commit this fix was applied on top of. Phase 6 diffs against exactly this, so it reviews what changed rather than the whole file.

worktree_path.description: The isolated worktree this lane ran in. Phase 5 lanes are file-disjoint AND worktree-isolated; two lanes sharing a checkout can each attribute a green suite to the other's patch.

verification.description: Machine evidence, not a claim. Counts are asserted against Phase 0's baseline: a batch that changes the test count without a stated reason fails Phase 6.

typecheck_errors.description: Errors reported by `pnpm typecheck` after the fix. Anything above 0 blocks the commit.

gates_tests.description: Total tests the run reported. Compared against the baseline count — a drop is behaviour loss until justified in `notes`.

gates_pass.description: Whether `pnpm gates` came back green. MUST be produced by `pnpm gates`, never `pnpm test`: only gates takes the machine-wide mutex at ~/.ledrums/locks/gates.lock, and concurrent unlocked sweeps have wedged this machine.

commands.description: Exactly what was run, so the evidence is reproducible. Verify the artifact, never the exit code.

interface_delta_actual.description: What the fix REALLY did to the public surface, measured after the fact. Phase 6 compares it against the finding's predicted interface_delta; a mismatch means the fix was not the fix that was approved.

commit_sha.description: Null until the batch is committed. Non-null asserts committed-HEAD green — the schema enforces that below. Presence on the remote is checked separately with `git ls-remote`, never from an agent's report.

notes.description: Anything a reviewer needs that the fields above do not carry — a deviation from the proposed fix, a zero-mutation no-op, a changed test count.

provenance.description: Who applied the fix. Stamped by the ORCHESTRATOR from the runtime pane footer, never self-reported — twux's EFFORT column records the launch flag, not the live tier.

review.description: Null while the fix is unreviewed; populated by Phase 6 ONLY. Two axes, from /code-review: Standards (does it follow this repo's documented standards?) and Spec (does it match what the finding asked for?). The reviewer MUST be a different model than provenance.model.

standards_verdict.description: clean = follows repo standards. findings = non-blocking issues worth recording. blocking = must not land as-is.

spec_verdict.description: clean = the diff is the finding's proposed_fix and nothing else. findings = drift worth recording. blocking = the fix does not do what was approved, or does more.

findings.description: Reviewer observations. A non-clean verdict with an empty array is invalid — the schema enforces it, so 'blocking' cannot be asserted without saying what blocks.

note.description: What is wrong and why it matters.

parity_check.description: Behaviour parity against Phase 0's baseline, not against intuition. Note that a green suite does NOT prove parity in a 0%-coverage region — for those the evidence is the import graph and git history.

reviewer.description: Reviewer provenance. Stamped by the orchestrator from the runtime footer.

allOf.description: ENFORCED: a committed fix asserts committed-HEAD green. Done = committed-HEAD green, not a lane's report.
ENFORCED: a non-clean review verdict must name at least one finding. Agreeing must not be the cheapest path, and 'blocking' with no reason is unactionable.
ENFORCED: a blocking review must name a blocking finding. A 'blocking' verdict whose worst finding is a nit is a mislabelled verdict.
